Commentary.Commentary: We're back. The players are taking the field. Rifat Beg and Zawad Abrar are the openers for Bangladesh Under-19.​ D. Deepesh to bowl the first over...
... CHASE BEGINS ...

There was a rain break at the 39-over mark, which reduced the match to 49-overs-a-side. As a result, the revised target for Bangladesh is 238 from 49 overs to win the game. Let's see how the chase pans out.

Abhigyan Kundu comes up for a quick chat. Says that he is happy with the score as the team had decided to aim for 230. He explains that the pitch is sticky and not easy to bat on, yet they manage to do well. He adds that he had a chat with Vaibhav, who told him to get his eye in while Vaibhav took care of the scoring. He feels that the practice he has done over the years has helped him.

For India, the batting innings was hampered by the regular fall of wickets. Even so, there was a superb knock from Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, who looked fluent and in full control. His partnerships with Vihaan Malhotra and then Abhigyan Kundu kept India on track. Once he departed, Bangladesh tightened the screws, and the run rate dipped, bringing pressure back into the game. Kanishk Chouhan showed positive intent to restore some momentum, while Abhigyan has carried on with a gritty effort at the other end.

A brilliant bowling display from Bangladesh. Al Fahad led the charge with a five-wicket haul, impressing one and all with his pace and clever variations. The Bangladesh skipper, Azizul Hakim Tamim, was equally sharp, nailing his bowling changes and field placements, and backing it up with his own spell of 2 for 42 from 10 overs.

Commentary.Commentary: Right then, we are done and dusted with the national anthems of both sides. All is in readiness here in Bulawayo as the action is about to begin. The sun is peeking through the clouds at the moment as the Indian openers, Ayush Mhatre and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, walk out to the centre. The Bangla boys get into a quick huddle before spreading on the ground. Two slips in place. Al Fahad is getting ready to bowl. Here we go...

Pitch report - Ed Rainsford says there is an 87 per cent chance of rain around. Informs that it is a brand new surface, similar to the last one, with a bit of grass and a few bare patches. He expects a two-paced pitch where some deliveries come nicely onto the bat, and others stop a touch. Feels that the quicks should enjoy their work, but batters who keep their heads early can still find plenty of runs.

Abhigyan Kundu comes up for a quick chat. Says that the team's motive was to stay in the contest and win the game against the USA, adding that they are here with the clear aim of lifting the cup. He mentions that watching Henil Patel bowl from behind the stumps is a great experience and that he enjoyed it thoroughly. Adds that when he walked out to bat during the chase, the coach's advice was to stay at the crease and play on the merit of the ball.

Ayush Mhatre, the captain of India Under-19, says that he wanted to bowl first because of the dampness in the wicket, but it's okay. He admits that the batting department is an area of concern as they should have finished the chase by losing fewer wickets, but adds that they will try to improve. He confirms that they are playing the same XI.

Zawad Abrar, who had come out for the toss instead of Azizul Hakim Tamim, says that the wicket looks damp and they want to take advantage of the first 10 to 15 overs. He adds that the team has prepared well and also did well in the Asia Cup.
